body:
Significant concerns. This change adds a `deploy()` helper that runs kubectl through a shell with the caller-supplied release tag interpolated into the command string, which is a shell command-injection vulnerability on the deploy host. The sibling `rollback()` already does the equivalent operation safely with an argv list, so the fix is small and the pattern is right there; neither new function has test coverage.

🤖 Generated with Claude

comments.body:
🔴 **CRITICAL:** `deploy()` builds a shell command with an f-string embedding the caller-supplied `tag` and runs it via `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)`. Any `tag` containing shell metacharacters (`;`, `&&`, `` ` ``, `$(...)`, `|`) is reinterpreted by the shell, so a tag pulled from a webhook, release name, PR title, or other CI-controlled input allows arbitrary command execution with the deploy process's credentials (often cluster-admin kubectl). Pass an argv list with no `shell=True` — matching `rollback()` immediately below — and ideally validate `tag` against a strict allowlist (e.g. a semver/tag regex) before use.

```suggestion
    subprocess.run(["kubectl", "set", "image", "deploy/api", f"api={tag}"], check=True)
```

🟢 **NIT:** Neither `deploy()` nor `rollback()` has test coverage. Both shell out to production kubectl, and a test that monkeypatches `subprocess.run` and asserts the exact argv would have caught the `shell=True` regression above. Consider adding one assertion per function pinning the constructed command.
